author: Literature Devil
description:
Milly Alcock says DC Studios’ new Supergirl movie isn’t centered around a man or romance. But why does Hollywood keep defining strong female characters by the love stories they refuse to have?

In this YouTube Short, I examine Milly Alcock’s Supergirl comments, Kara Zor-El, the James Gunn DCU, and a wider trend in Hollywood writing—while comparing her with male heroes like Odysseus and John Wick, whose love for a woman strengthens rather than diminishes them.

Does removing romance make a female hero more credible—or is Hollywood mistaking love for weakness?

#Supergirl #MillyAlcock #DCU #FilmCommentary #Shorts
title: Supergirl Don't Need No Man? | Hollywood’s Strange Trend

author: Literature Devil
description:
Why is “Hellfire” Disney’s darkest villain song?

In Disney’s The Hunchback of Notre Dame, Judge Claude Frollo believes himself to be a righteous man fighting vice and corruption. But when his desire for Esmeralda clashes with that righteous self-image, Frollo refuses to confront his own hypocrisy—and instead embraces evil.

This short character analysis explains the meaning of “Hellfire,” Frollo’s descent into madness, and the moment he crosses the moral event horizon.

What do you think is Disney’s darkest villain song?

Subscribe for more movie analysis, character studies, storytelling breakdowns, and video essays.

#Hellfire #DisneyVillains #TheHunchbackOfNotreDame
title: Why Hellfire is the Darkest Disney Song
